correctness.rationale: Substituting N(x)=phi(x)u into Nijenhuis torsion gives phi(x)psi(y)-phi(y)psi(x)=phi(u)phi([x,y]), psi=phi([u,x]). If phi(Z)=0 both vanish. Otherwise projection ker(phi)->V is onto and its brackets span Z; choosing two vectors in ker(phi) with nonzero phi bracket forces phi(u)=0, then substituting a central z with phi(z)!=0 gives psi=0. For u=v+z, if v=0 the central u and phiZ counts give q^n(q^c-1)(q^{c-1}-1); if v!=0, the map w->v wedge w has rank n-1, so phiZ choices q^{c-n+1}-1 and z fiber q^{c-1}, yielding (q^n-1)q^{m-1}(q^{c-n+1}-1). Add phiZ=0 (q^m-1)(q^n-1) and divide by q-1 scalar representations. N^2=phi(u)N establishes non-square-zero count; fixed q asymptotic follows from q^{c-n} growth. Independent small finite checks n=2,3 at q=2,3 corroborate; n=2 has no second type, n>=3 admits one.
